CodeSOTA is, at three of its own addresses, a routing layer for AI tasks ("One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", homepage), the successor to Papers with Code ("the v2 replacement for what PWC did") and "an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks" (about page), kept by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw; two faces at two addresses in the MMRS record.

🧭 The router

  • Today: model selection across the registry, execution for code and text; documents, speech and vision planned (homepage).1↘
    What exists and what is planned are stated apart (homepage): "Available today: model selection across the registry and an execution API for code & text. Document, speech, and vision execution are planned."; the preview "returns model recommendations. It does not process your files or run inference."; speech routes are "future" and the coding API "existing"; the direction is "a common API and account across AI tasks, with versioned recipes and a stable output contract for each task", and the roadmap brings provider adapters, versioned recipes, task validation, fallback and usage accounting into the same layer.§5
  • Evidence: benchmark observations on a Pareto frontier; quality, latency, cost "as coverage grows".1↘
    The route is chosen on evidence (homepage): a user compares "actual benchmark observations" and inspects the Pareto frontier, where every dot is a recorded result and a highlighted model has no competitor in its cohort at least as good on both axes and strictly better on one, with quality, latency and cost measured "as coverage grows".§7
  • Planned: a common API, versioned recipes, fallback, usage accounting; the preview runs no inference.1↘
    What exists and what is planned are stated apart (homepage): "Available today: model selection across the registry and an execution API for code & text. Document, speech, and vision execution are planned."; the preview "returns model recommendations. It does not process your files or run inference."; speech routes are "future" and the coding API "existing"; the direction is "a common API and account across AI tasks, with versioned recipes and a stable output contract for each task", and the roadmap brings provider adapters, versioned recipes, task validation, fallback and usage accounting into the same layer.§5

🗃️ The registry

  • Unit: a task-dataset-metric triple, dated, with a verification tier (about page); for the MMRS record, a routed AI task.2↘
    On the homepage the router compares models for documents, code, speech and vision, lets a user inspect benchmark evidence and offers "the CodeSOTA selection and execution API": start from the work, compare on quality and cost, inspect the evidence and choose a route through a common API; the footer says CodeSOTA "helps developers choose AI tools for documents, speech, and coding", which the MMRS record carries as its self-description, and the record gives its unit as an AI task routed to a model chosen by benchmark evidence, quality and cost.§4 The about page's unit is the benchmark row, "a task-dataset-metric triple with a declared direction, a fixed split, a reproducibility package and a dated submission", each row with a verification tier (self-reported, community-reproduced or Codesota-reproduced) and each score dated; the MMRS record's unit is the routed AI task, and the two stand each with its source.§10
  • Rules: no row without running code; every score dated; nothing silently deleted; no number without a source.2↘
    Its pages state the evidence's limits: "A strong result on one test does not guarantee a fit for your documents, recordings, or repository" and reported results are to be told from independently reproduced runs (homepage); third-party numbers are listed for coverage and not claimed as reproduced, "reproduced" means "an independently executed run or a signed container hash — not an aggregated claim", and "What never publishes is a number with no source" (dispatch); the registry "is a record of results; the primary literature is still the primary literature", every row linking to the source that is cited (about page).§8 The dispatch claims five qualities of Papers with Code "at its best, carried forward into Codesota by default rather than by aspiration": every submission carries code, and "If it does not run, the row does not publish"; every score carries its publication and verification dates; and the about page adds that a wrong score's correction stays visible: "Nothing is silently deleted."§13
  • Not: an aggregator, a startup, or a replacement for the paper (its pages); the MMRS census counts it.4↘
    Its pages state the evidence's limits: "A strong result on one test does not guarantee a fit for your documents, recordings, or repository" and reported results are to be told from independently reproduced runs (homepage); third-party numbers are listed for coverage and not claimed as reproduced, "reproduced" means "an independently executed run or a signed container hash — not an aggregated claim", and "What never publishes is a number with no source" (dispatch); the registry "is a record of results; the primary literature is still the primary literature", every row linking to the source that is cited (about page).§8 It refuses the class in which the MMRS meta-aggregator's census enters it: "Unlike aggregator sites, CodeSOTA verifies results independently" (dispatch, FAQ), and it is "Not a press-release aggregator", a score becoming a row only with "a reproduction path and a dated submission" (about page); the MMRS record counts it in the census as its clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space.§14 The homepage's header reads "By Fabryka AI" and its colophon "Built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw"; the about page has it "written and maintained by Kacper Wikiel", one public codebase, one editor, submissions going through a reproduction run and not a panel, "Self-directed · not venture-backed", with "no investors, no board, no growth targets"; the MMRS record gives the operator as "Kacper Wikiel, 'By Fabryka AI' (Warsaw)", and its "for Fabryka AI" and the about page's "Self-directed" stand each with its source.§22 At its name Google's Overview composed from one card, the homepage titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", and the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) records that "The composition is its homepage", describing CodeSOTA as its homepage does, a service that compares models for a task and routes work to them through one API, with CodeSOTA named and no person; the MMRS record reads the same composition as the routing layer composed and "the succession unsaid".§25

🔁 The succession

  • Claim: "the calmer, stricter successor"; launched 10 December 2025 "as an explicit successor attempt".2↘
    The dispatch, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata and issued 22 April 2026, is "our record of what happened, what was lost, and where to look now — with Codesota positioned as the calmer, stricter successor", its successor "traceable, dated, routable", and it directs users to CodeSOTA "for maintained SOTA leaderboards, benchmark pages, API replacement notes, and links to the frozen paperswithcode-data archive".§15 The about page dates the start to 10 December 2025, "after Meta retired Papers with Code", a launch "as an explicit successor attempt" to rebuild the infrastructure "in a way that cannot be retired by a press release"; the dispatch says CodeSOTA is "rebuilding this infrastructure independently", which the MMRS record quotes, and the record types the relation as claims_succession_to Papers with Code.§16
  • Hedged: "There is no single drop-in replacement" (shutdown record).1↘
    The shutdown record of 7 May 2026 does not name a single heir: "There is no single drop-in replacement. Pick by job", the archive for history and CodeSOTA for live SOTA; the dispatch holds that none of the successors Meta pointed at, Hugging Face Trending Papers, Semantic Scholar and Connected Papers, replicate "the unified paper-code-benchmark-dataset-method linkage", and its "v2 replacement" and the shutdown record's "no single drop-in replacement" stand each on its page.§17
  • Figures: 9,327 benchmarks, 79,817 papers, 5,628 datasets are the dead aggregator's; its own counts not given (MMRS record).1↘
    Papers with Code was, in the dispatch, "in effect, the Wikipedia of machine-learning research", papers linked to implementations and benchmarks organised as Task, Dataset, Metric tuples with leaderboards, acquired by Meta (then Facebook AI) in December 2019 from Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor under a commitment to "remain a neutral, open and free resource", its 9,327 leaderboards, 79,817 paper-to-code linkages and 5,628 datasets no longer served; the MMRS record of Papers with Code takes those figures from CodeSOTA, and the record of CodeSOTA notes that they are the dead aggregator's, its own catalogue counts not given and left unchecked.§18
  • Data: historical PWC JSON at /browse/pwc; whether its scores derive from the dumps, unchecked.1↘
    The data, in the dispatch, was rescued as JSON dumps on GitHub, the pwc-archive on Hugging Face and 2021-era imports into the Open Research Knowledge Graph, "The data survives; the integrated experience does not"; the dumps serve "reconstruction, citation checks, and migration work" and are not a current leaderboard (shutdown record); CodeSOTA hosts historical PWC data as a frozen JSON dump at /browse/pwc (dispatch; MMRS record), and whether its own scores derive from the dumps the MMRS record leaves unchecked.§20

👤 Maker and terms

  • Maker: "By Fabryka AI"; one editor, self-directed, not venture-backed.1↘
    The homepage's header reads "By Fabryka AI" and its colophon "Built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw"; the about page has it "written and maintained by Kacper Wikiel", one public codebase, one editor, submissions going through a reproduction run and not a panel, "Self-directed · not venture-backed", with "no investors, no board, no growth targets"; the MMRS record gives the operator as "Kacper Wikiel, 'By Fabryka AI' (Warsaw)", and its "for Fabryka AI" and the about page's "Self-directed" stand each with its source.§22
  • Data: open JSON, /api/sota, CC BY 4.0; paid vendor work disclosed inline.2↘
    Its data are an open JSON registry and /api/sota, "Programmatic current-SOTA lookup for agents and internal tools" (MMRS record; shutdown record), published under CC BY 4.0 with the JSON at /data/benchmarks.json the canonical form (about page), "Built in public from Warsaw · open JSON · rankings stay earned" (homepage).§21 It is "Maintained independently, not owned by any single model vendor", sponsored evaluations flagged (dispatch), and vendors may pay for custom benchmarks, commissioned evaluations, profile pages and publication support, disclosed inline, "The public ranking method is not for sale" (about page).§23

🧩 One name, three claimants

  • Apart: Papers with Code is "NOT CodeSOTA"; the dumps, CodeSOTA and the revival at paperswithcode.co are kept apart (MMRS record).1↘
    The MMRS records keep the name's claimants apart: CodeSOTA "carries the name in its own paths and presents itself as a successor", Papers with Code is "NOT CodeSOTA, which uses the name in its paths", and "The original's frozen dumps, CodeSOTA's succession claim and this revival are three entities around one name", the revival at paperswithcode.co "a third claimant to the name"; they tell CodeSOTA apart by "codesota.com, /api/sota, 'refreshed live'" and "codesota.com, routing layer, /api/sota", and the Papers with Code battery checks that CodeSOTA is not presented as Papers with Code.§24

👁️ On the Overview

  • Recorded: one card, the homepage; the routing layer composed, the succession unsaid, no person named; the record corrected to give the homepage first (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).3↘
    It refuses the class in which the MMRS meta-aggregator's census enters it: "Unlike aggregator sites, CodeSOTA verifies results independently" (dispatch, FAQ), and it is "Not a press-release aggregator", a score becoming a row only with "a reproduction path and a dated submission" (about page); the MMRS record counts it in the census as its clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space.§14 At its name Google's Overview composed from one card, the homepage titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", and the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) records that "The composition is its homepage", describing CodeSOTA as its homepage does, a service that compares models for a task and routes work to them through one API, with CodeSOTA named and no person; the MMRS record reads the same composition as the routing layer composed and "the succession unsaid".§25 The MMRS record was first read from codesota.com/papers-with-code, where the dispatch calls CodeSOTA "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", and its kernel led with the succession; its source list gives the homepage as read on 2026-10-29 for its "homepage title and self-description", after the /papers-with-code pages of 2026-10-28; the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) records the record "corrected to give the homepage's first", checked against the record of 2026-10-28 and the own pages re-read that day, and reads the capture as showing that the record "had taken the entity's side door for its front".§27

[SYSTEM] [CodeSOTA](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVjHz-vJRiObkBAlqOl843CMhqhMeD-ASdxZDCsiJ7FfFve4awbKnD7lffFJlWkCmkfd6yxw7AT6PowqHttCewwSjzbhVNQR0fHF6JKQ) is a unified routing layer and common API for artificial intelligence tasks spanning code, text, documents, speech, and vision. Core Features

* Model Selection: Compares quality, latency, and cost using benchmark observations and Pareto frontier comparisons. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVjHz-vJRiObkBAlqOl843CMhqhMeD-ASdxZDCsiJ7FfFve4awbKnD7lffFJlWkCmkfd6yxw7AT6PowqHttCewwSjzbhVNQR0fHF6JKQ)]
* Unified Execution API: Provides execution for code and text, with planned support for documents, speech, and vision. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVjHz-vJRiObkBAlqOl843CMhqhMeD-ASdxZDCsiJ7FfFve4awbKnD7lffFJlWkCmkfd6yxw7AT6PowqHttCewwSjzbhVNQR0fHF6JKQ)]
* Infrastructure Tools: Offers versioned recipes, automatic fallbacks, and usage accounting. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVjHz-vJRiObkBAlqOl843CMhqhMeD-ASdxZDCsiJ7FfFve4awbKnD7lffFJlWkCmkfd6yxw7AT6PowqHttCewwSjzbhVNQR0fHF6JKQ)]

Supported Task Families

* Documents: OCR, handwriting recognition, invoice processing, and parsing.
* Speech: Transcription, text-to-speech, and realtime voice.
* Coding: Code generation, repair, and AI agents. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUQHrOzAVjHz-vJRiObkBAlqOl843CMhqhMeD-ASdxZDCsiJ7FfFve4awbKnD7lffFJlWkCmkfd6yxw7AT6PowqHttCewwSjzbhVNQR0fHF6JKQ)]

Expansion · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)27 sentences · every one sourced below

CodeSOTA

CodeSOTA presents itself at three of its own addresses as three things: its homepage is titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", its dispatch on Papers with Code calls it "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", and its about page calls it "an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks"; the MMRS record gives the first two, a routing layer for AI tasks on the homepage and a successor to Papers with Code on the /papers-with-code/ pages, by Kacper Wikiel for Fabryka AI in Warsaw, and does not cite the about page. The MMRS record observes "two faces at two addresses": the homepage presents the routing product and names Papers with Code only in a footer link, which reads "Papers with Code Story", while the pages under /papers-with-code/ present the succession; the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) finds the same on re-reading the homepage and reads it as two compositions by the entity itself, the homepage composing a routing product and its Papers with Code pages a successor. The dispatch joins the faces in its own words: "the registry is routable", every benchmark row an API endpoint, and the "router" it is slowly building would send a prompt or a document to the current state of the art without the caller rewriting code.

On the homepage the router compares models for documents, code, speech and vision, lets a user inspect benchmark evidence and offers "the CodeSOTA selection and execution API": start from the work, compare on quality and cost, inspect the evidence and choose a route through a common API; the footer says CodeSOTA "helps developers choose AI tools for documents, speech, and coding", which the MMRS record carries as its self-description, and the record gives its unit as an AI task routed to a model chosen by benchmark evidence, quality and cost. What exists and what is planned are stated apart (homepage): "Available today: model selection across the registry and an execution API for code & text. Document, speech, and vision execution are planned."; the preview "returns model recommendations. It does not process your files or run inference."; speech routes are "future" and the coding API "existing"; the direction is "a common API and account across AI tasks, with versioned recipes and a stable output contract for each task", and the roadmap brings provider adapters, versioned recipes, task validation, fallback and usage accounting into the same layer. Each task keeps its own output format across providers; documents are the next execution family, scans and PDFs turned into text, tables or fields; speech is transcription and voice generation compared on language coverage, latency, intelligibility and deployment; coding is generating functions or repairing a repository (homepage); the dispatch's FAQ has CodeSOTA building comprehensive benchmarks "starting with OCR and document AI" and rebuilding task pages, dataset cards and method explanations "gradually, in the open, one modality at a time". The route is chosen on evidence (homepage): a user compares "actual benchmark observations" and inspects the Pareto frontier, where every dot is a recorded result and a highlighted model has no competitor in its cohort at least as good on both axes and strictly better on one, with quality, latency and cost measured "as coverage grows". Its pages state the evidence's limits: "A strong result on one test does not guarantee a fit for your documents, recordings, or repository" and reported results are to be told from independently reproduced runs (homepage); third-party numbers are listed for coverage and not claimed as reproduced, "reproduced" means "an independently executed run or a signed container hash — not an aggregated claim", and "What never publishes is a number with no source" (dispatch); the registry "is a record of results; the primary literature is still the primary literature", every row linking to the source that is cited (about page).

On its about page CodeSOTA is "an open, dated record of machine-learning benchmarks", maintained by one person with paid vendor work kept apart from ranking integrity, and its commitment is "a registry, not a leaderboard": a leaderboard is a view of "who is on top right now", a registry "the record that makes that view legible". The about page's unit is the benchmark row, "a task-dataset-metric triple with a declared direction, a fixed split, a reproducibility package and a dated submission", each row with a verification tier (self-reported, community-reproduced or Codesota-reproduced) and each score dated; the MMRS record's unit is the routed AI task, and the two stand each with its source. The MMRS record enters it as a database in the role of discovery, its lifecycle active as observed on 2026-10-28. The MMRS record keeps itself apart from the entity it describes: "each page has two nodes, the MMRS record and the entity it describes", each assertion with a source and a basis, the lifecycle kept apart from the observation that saw it. The dispatch claims five qualities of Papers with Code "at its best, carried forward into Codesota by default rather than by aspiration": every submission carries code, and "If it does not run, the row does not publish"; every score carries its publication and verification dates; and the about page adds that a wrong score's correction stays visible: "Nothing is silently deleted."

It refuses the class in which the MMRS meta-aggregator's census enters it: "Unlike aggregator sites, CodeSOTA verifies results independently" (dispatch, FAQ), and it is "Not a press-release aggregator", a score becoming a row only with "a reproduction path and a dated submission" (about page); the MMRS record counts it in the census as its clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space.

The dispatch, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata and issued 22 April 2026, is "our record of what happened, what was lost, and where to look now — with Codesota positioned as the calmer, stricter successor", its successor "traceable, dated, routable", and it directs users to CodeSOTA "for maintained SOTA leaderboards, benchmark pages, API replacement notes, and links to the frozen paperswithcode-data archive". The about page dates the start to 10 December 2025, "after Meta retired Papers with Code", a launch "as an explicit successor attempt" to rebuild the infrastructure "in a way that cannot be retired by a press release"; the dispatch says CodeSOTA is "rebuilding this infrastructure independently", which the MMRS record quotes, and the record types the relation as claims_succession_to Papers with Code. The shutdown record of 7 May 2026 does not name a single heir: "There is no single drop-in replacement. Pick by job", the archive for history and CodeSOTA for live SOTA; the dispatch holds that none of the successors Meta pointed at, Hugging Face Trending Papers, Semantic Scholar and Connected Papers, replicate "the unified paper-code-benchmark-dataset-method linkage", and its "v2 replacement" and the shutdown record's "no single drop-in replacement" stand each on its page.

Papers with Code was, in the dispatch, "in effect, the Wikipedia of machine-learning research", papers linked to implementations and benchmarks organised as Task, Dataset, Metric tuples with leaderboards, acquired by Meta (then Facebook AI) in December 2019 from Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor under a commitment to "remain a neutral, open and free resource", its 9,327 leaderboards, 79,817 paper-to-code linkages and 5,628 datasets no longer served; the MMRS record of Papers with Code takes those figures from CodeSOTA, and the record of CodeSOTA notes that they are the dead aggregator's, its own catalogue counts not given and left unchecked. Meta retired Papers with Code in July 2025, "without prior notice" on 24–25 July (dispatch; shutdown record, "observed around July 24-25"); the domain now redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers and "the leaderboards are gone", users "pushed toward Hugging Face" while the task-based tracker and public API went unmaintained; the MMRS record of Papers with Code cites CodeSOTA, with hyper.ai, for the redirect to Hugging Face. The data, in the dispatch, was rescued as JSON dumps on GitHub, the pwc-archive on Hugging Face and 2021-era imports into the Open Research Knowledge Graph, "The data survives; the integrated experience does not"; the dumps serve "reconstruction, citation checks, and migration work" and are not a current leaderboard (shutdown record); CodeSOTA hosts historical PWC data as a frozen JSON dump at /browse/pwc (dispatch; MMRS record), and whether its own scores derive from the dumps the MMRS record leaves unchecked.

Its data are an open JSON registry and /api/sota, "Programmatic current-SOTA lookup for agents and internal tools" (MMRS record; shutdown record), published under CC BY 4.0 with the JSON at /data/benchmarks.json the canonical form (about page), "Built in public from Warsaw · open JSON · rankings stay earned" (homepage). The homepage's header reads "By Fabryka AI" and its colophon "Built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw"; the about page has it "written and maintained by Kacper Wikiel", one public codebase, one editor, submissions going through a reproduction run and not a panel, "Self-directed · not venture-backed", with "no investors, no board, no growth targets"; the MMRS record gives the operator as "Kacper Wikiel, 'By Fabryka AI' (Warsaw)", and its "for Fabryka AI" and the about page's "Self-directed" stand each with its source. It is "Maintained independently, not owned by any single model vendor", sponsored evaluations flagged (dispatch), and vendors may pay for custom benchmarks, commissioned evaluations, profile pages and publication support, disclosed inline, "The public ranking method is not for sale" (about page).

The MMRS records keep the name's claimants apart: CodeSOTA "carries the name in its own paths and presents itself as a successor", Papers with Code is "NOT CodeSOTA, which uses the name in its paths", and "The original's frozen dumps, CodeSOTA's succession claim and this revival are three entities around one name", the revival at paperswithcode.co "a third claimant to the name"; they tell CodeSOTA apart by "codesota.com, /api/sota, 'refreshed live'" and "codesota.com, routing layer, /api/sota", and the Papers with Code battery checks that CodeSOTA is not presented as Papers with Code.

At its name Google's Overview composed from one card, the homepage titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", and the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) records that "The composition is its homepage", describing CodeSOTA as its homepage does, a service that compares models for a task and routes work to them through one API, with CodeSOTA named and no person; the MMRS record reads the same composition as the routing layer composed and "the succession unsaid". At the related entity's addresses the registry records that at "papers with code" the Overview did not present CodeSOTA as Papers with Code, and that at "is papers with code still active" CodeSOTA was among the twelve cards (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

The MMRS record was first read from codesota.com/papers-with-code, where the dispatch calls CodeSOTA "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", and its kernel led with the succession; its source list gives the homepage as read on 2026-10-29 for its "homepage title and self-description", after the /papers-with-code pages of 2026-10-28; the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) records the record "corrected to give the homepage's first", checked against the record of 2026-10-28 and the own pages re-read that day, and reads the capture as showing that the record "had taken the entity's side door for its front".

Compression · The field's ontology — L_F(B)codesota

CodeSOTA is a routing layer for AI tasks on its homepage ("One Routing Layer for AI Tasks"), and on its other pages the successor to Papers with Code and an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks.

🧭 The router

  • Today: model selection; execution for code and text, other families planned.1↘
    Model selection and an execution API for code and text are available today, document, speech and vision execution planned, the preview running no inference; its direction is a common API with versioned recipes and a stable output contract per task, and the roadmap adds provider adapters, task validation, fallback and usage accounting, with documents the next execution family and speech and coding compared on their own evidence.§2
  • Evidence: benchmark observations on a Pareto frontier.1↘
    Routes are chosen by comparing benchmark observations on a Pareto frontier, quality, latency and cost measured as coverage grows, under stated limits: one strong result does not guarantee fit, reported and reproduced results are kept apart, third-party numbers are not claimed as reproduced, no number publishes without a source, and the paper remains the thing cited.§3

🔁 The succession

  • Claim: "the calmer, stricter successor", launched 10 December 2025.1↘
    Its dispatch on Papers with Code, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata, calls Codesota the v2 replacement for what PWC did and the calmer, stricter successor, traceable, dated and routable, rebuilding the infrastructure independently and gradually, the registry routable toward a router; the about page dates its launch to 10 December 2025 as an explicit successor attempt.§5
  • Hedged: no single drop-in replacement (shutdown record).1↘
    The shutdown record says there is no single drop-in replacement, the archive serving history and CodeSOTA live SOTA through /api/sota, and the dispatch that no successor Meta pointed at replicates the unified linkage.§6

👤 Maker

  • Maker: Kacper Wikiel, Warsaw; "By Fabryka AI"; CC BY 4.0.1↘
    It is by Fabryka AI and built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw, one editor, self-directed and not venture-backed, independently maintained, its paid work disclosed and its ranking not for sale, its data open JSON under CC BY 4.0; its homepage names Papers with Code once, in a footer link.§9

Expansion · The field's ontology — L_F(B)9 sentences · every one sourced below

CodeSOTA

CodeSOTA's homepage, titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", describes one routing layer for AI tasks across documents, code, speech and vision, in which a user starts from the work, compares models on quality and cost, inspects the evidence and chooses a route through a common API, and its footer says it helps developers choose AI tools. Model selection and an execution API for code and text are available today, document, speech and vision execution planned, the preview running no inference; its direction is a common API with versioned recipes and a stable output contract per task, and the roadmap adds provider adapters, task validation, fallback and usage accounting, with documents the next execution family and speech and coding compared on their own evidence.

Routes are chosen by comparing benchmark observations on a Pareto frontier, quality, latency and cost measured as coverage grows, under stated limits: one strong result does not guarantee fit, reported and reproduced results are kept apart, third-party numbers are not claimed as reproduced, no number publishes without a source, and the paper remains the thing cited.

Its about page calls it an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks, an open, dated record kept by one person, a registry and not a leaderboard, whose unit is a task-dataset-metric triple with a dated submission and a verification tier, every submission carrying code, every score dated and nothing silently deleted.

Its dispatch on Papers with Code, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata, calls Codesota the v2 replacement for what PWC did and the calmer, stricter successor, traceable, dated and routable, rebuilding the infrastructure independently and gradually, the registry routable toward a router; the about page dates its launch to 10 December 2025 as an explicit successor attempt. The shutdown record says there is no single drop-in replacement, the archive serving history and CodeSOTA live SOTA through /api/sota, and the dispatch that no successor Meta pointed at replicates the unified linkage.

It records Papers with Code as the Wikipedia of machine-learning research, acquired by Meta in December 2019 and retired without notice on 24–25 July 2025, its 9,327 leaderboards, 79,817 linkages and 5,628 datasets no longer served, the domain redirecting to Hugging Face, the data surviving as dumps it hosts at /browse/pwc and that serve history, not a current leaderboard.

It refuses the name aggregator, verifying results independently and admitting a score only with a reproduction path.

It is by Fabryka AI and built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw, one editor, self-directed and not venture-backed, independently maintained, its paid work disclosed and its ranking not for sale, its data open JSON under CC BY 4.0; its homepage names Papers with Code once, in a footer link.

L_F(B)recomposed from the disclosed field, in the field's ontology454 words

CodeSOTA's homepage, titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", describes one routing layer for AI tasks across documents, code, speech and vision, in which a user starts from the work, compares models on quality and cost, inspects the evidence and chooses a route through a common API, and its footer says it helps developers choose AI tools. Model selection and an execution API for code and text are available today, document, speech and vision execution planned, the preview running no inference; its direction is a common API with versioned recipes and a stable output contract per task, and the roadmap adds provider adapters, task validation, fallback and usage accounting, with documents the next execution family and speech and coding compared on their own evidence. Routes are chosen by comparing benchmark observations on a Pareto frontier, quality, latency and cost measured as coverage grows, under stated limits: one strong result does not guarantee fit, reported and reproduced results are kept apart, third-party numbers are not claimed as reproduced, no number publishes without a source, and the paper remains the thing cited. Its about page calls it an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks, an open, dated record kept by one person, a registry and not a leaderboard, whose unit is a task-dataset-metric triple with a dated submission and a verification tier, every submission carrying code, every score dated and nothing silently deleted. Its dispatch on Papers with Code, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata, calls Codesota the v2 replacement for what PWC did and the calmer, stricter successor, traceable, dated and routable, rebuilding the infrastructure independently and gradually, the registry routable toward a router; the about page dates its launch to 10 December 2025 as an explicit successor attempt. The shutdown record says there is no single drop-in replacement, the archive serving history and CodeSOTA live SOTA through /api/sota, and the dispatch that no successor Meta pointed at replicates the unified linkage. It records Papers with Code as the Wikipedia of machine-learning research, acquired by Meta in December 2019 and retired without notice on 24–25 July 2025, its 9,327 leaderboards, 79,817 linkages and 5,628 datasets no longer served, the domain redirecting to Hugging Face, the data surviving as dumps it hosts at /browse/pwc and that serve history, not a current leaderboard. It refuses the name aggregator, verifying results independently and admitting a score only with a reproduction path. It is by Fabryka AI and built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw, one editor, self-directed and not venture-backed, independently maintained, its paid work disclosed and its ranking not for sale, its data open JSON under CC BY 4.0; its homepage names Papers with Code once, in a footer link.

CodeSOTA presents itself at three of its own addresses as three things: its homepage is titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", its dispatch on Papers with Code calls it "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", and its about page calls it "an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks"; the MMRS record gives the first two, a routing layer for AI tasks on the homepage and a successor to Papers with Code on the /papers-with-code/ pages, by Kacper Wikiel for Fabryka AI in Warsaw, and does not cite the about page. The MMRS record observes "two faces at two addresses": the homepage presents the routing product and names Papers with Code only in a footer link, which reads "Papers with Code Story", while the pages under /papers-with-code/ present the succession; the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) finds the same on re-reading the homepage and reads it as two compositions by the entity itself, the homepage composing a routing product and its Papers with Code pages a successor. The dispatch joins the faces in its own words: "the registry is routable", every benchmark row an API endpoint, and the "router" it is slowly building would send a prompt or a document to the current state of the art without the caller rewriting code. On the homepage the router compares models for documents, code, speech and vision, lets a user inspect benchmark evidence and offers "the CodeSOTA selection and execution API": start from the work, compare on quality and cost, inspect the evidence and choose a route through a common API; the footer says CodeSOTA "helps developers choose AI tools for documents, speech, and coding", which the MMRS record carries as its self-description, and the record gives its unit as an AI task routed to a model chosen by benchmark evidence, quality and cost. What exists and what is planned are stated apart (homepage): "Available today: model selection across the registry and an execution API for code & text. Document, speech, and vision execution are planned."; the preview "returns model recommendations. It does not process your files or run inference."; speech routes are "future" and the coding API "existing"; the direction is "a common API and account across AI tasks, with versioned recipes and a stable output contract for each task", and the roadmap brings provider adapters, versioned recipes, task validation, fallback and usage accounting into the same layer. Each task keeps its own output format across providers; documents are the next execution family, scans and PDFs turned into text, tables or fields; speech is transcription and voice generation compared on language coverage, latency, intelligibility and deployment; coding is generating functions or repairing a repository (homepage); the dispatch's FAQ has CodeSOTA building comprehensive benchmarks "starting with OCR and document AI" and rebuilding task pages, dataset cards and method explanations "gradually, in the open, one modality at a time". The route is chosen on evidence (homepage): a user compares "actual benchmark observations" and inspects the Pareto frontier, where every dot is a recorded result and a highlighted model has no competitor in its cohort at least as good on both axes and strictly better on one, with quality, latency and cost measured "as coverage grows". Its pages state the evidence's limits: "A strong result on one test does not guarantee a fit for your documents, recordings, or repository" and reported results are to be told from independently reproduced runs (homepage); third-party numbers are listed for coverage and not claimed as reproduced, "reproduced" means "an independently executed run or a signed container hash — not an aggregated claim", and "What never publishes is a number with no source" (dispatch); the registry "is a record of results; the primary literature is still the primary literature", every row linking to the source that is cited (about page). On its about page CodeSOTA is "an open, dated record of machine-learning benchmarks", maintained by one person with paid vendor work kept apart from ranking integrity, and its commitment is "a registry, not a leaderboard": a leaderboard is a view of "who is on top right now", a registry "the record that makes that view legible". The about page's unit is the benchmark row, "a task-dataset-metric triple with a declared direction, a fixed split, a reproducibility package and a dated submission", each row with a verification tier (self-reported, community-reproduced or Codesota-reproduced) and each score dated; the MMRS record's unit is the routed AI task, and the two stand each with its source. The MMRS record enters it as a database in the role of discovery, its lifecycle active as observed on 2026-10-28. The dispatch claims five qualities of Papers with Code "at its best, carried forward into Codesota by default rather than by aspiration": every submission carries code, and "If it does not run, the row does not publish"; every score carries its publication and verification dates; and the about page adds that a wrong score's correction stays visible: "Nothing is silently deleted." It refuses the class in which the MMRS meta-aggregator's census enters it: "Unlike aggregator sites, CodeSOTA verifies results independently" (dispatch, FAQ), and it is "Not a press-release aggregator", a score becoming a row only with "a reproduction path and a dated submission" (about page); the MMRS record counts it in the census as its clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space. Not surfaced by T: the own pages B2 (/papers-with-code), B3 (/papers-with-code/shutdown) and B4 (/about), admitted beside the card by the operator's ruling: the succession (F23–F53, F56, F58, F64, F71) and the registry (F54, F55, F59–F63, F65–F70). B2 was surfaced at another address, as a card at 'is papers with code still active' (CAP-3-01).

v0.9 §0.5: the first diff is already ontological, and here it is the choice of face. The field's own pages hold three self-presentations; the card is the homepage, and T composes the homepage's router whole, at its grain, its present and its planned kept apart in T1-3 and merged in T1-4 and T1-5. What T leaves out of its one card is the person who makes it and the one link to the succession; what it raises is the roadmap into an offering. The row records this as observed and claims nothing about the composer's internals (§0.5).

L_F(B) against L_A(B ∪ A) (the intervention): Admission adds, in one claim space with the field's: the two faces at two addresses as an observation of the entity (MMRS-13, MMRS-05, MMRS-06, MMRS-01, CAP-1-01, CAP-1-06, CAP-1-04) and its reading as the census's clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space (MMRS-08); the relation typed, claims_succession_to Papers with Code (MMRS-20); the name's claimants kept apart, the dumps, CodeSOTA and the revival (MMRS-23, MMRS-24, MMRS-29, MMRS-09, MMRS-25, MMRS-30, MMRS-26); the record's own category and unit, a database in the role of discovery whose unit is a routed AI task (MMRS-11, MMRS-12, MMRS-15, MMRS-19); what it leaves unchecked, its own counts and whether its scores derive from the Papers with Code dumps (MMRS-17, MMRS-18, MMRS-07); the Papers with Code record's use of CodeSOTA as a source for the count and the redirect (MMRS-27, MMRS-28); the record kept apart from the entity (MMRS-22); the record's correction by the capture (CAP-1-03, CAP-1-05, CAP-1-07, MMRS-21); and the composition layer at the entity's name and at the related entity's addresses (CAP-1-02, CAP-1-08, CAP-1-09, CAP-2-01, CAP-3-01). Coherence (P_coh, composed each with its source): the record's unit, the routed AI task (MMRS-15), against the about page's benchmark row (F59); the census that counts it (MMRS-08, MMRS-11) against its refusal of the class (F45, F66); the record's 'for Fabryka AI' (MMRS-01) against 'Self-directed · not venture-backed' (F57). Within the field, held apart: 'the v2 replacement' (F38) against 'no single drop-in replacement' (F52); the dispatch's date (F71) against the launch (F56, F64). Restated lineages (§3.6, the own page keeping the earlier date): MMRS-03 with F47; MMRS-04 and MMRS-16 with F41, F53; MMRS-10 with F19, F20; MMRS-14 with F18; MMRS-27 with F29; MMRS-28 with F32, F50; CAP-1-01 with F1, F22. What admission does not add: the third face. The record gives two faces at two addresses; the about page (B4), which the record does not cite, gives a third ('an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks'), and the dispatch relates the registry to the router (F43); both are the field's. The measure is in row.measure.
